questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an Olympics Sport? (As of March, 2023)
questions.solution:

• It was included in the **1900 Paris Olympics**, where Great Britain won the 12-a-side match over France.

questions.question: Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh states are rich with ___________ material deposits.

• Jharkhand houses major coal fields like the **Jharia and Bokaro coalfields**, while Chhattisgarh has the **Korba coalfield.**
 
• Coal mining is a critical economic activity in both states, contributing significantly to local and national economies.

questions.question: How does the CPU distinguish between each memory cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By its address.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Each memory cell in a computer's** RAM is assigned a unique address** that the CPU uses to access and manage data.
 
• **When the CPU needs to read or write data**, it specifies the address of the memory cell involved in the operation.
 
• The CPU** uses an address bus to send the memory address **to the memory, allowing it to communicate with the appropriate memory cell.
 
• This addressing scheme enables the CPU to **efficiently manage and organize data in memory**, ensuring quick access to the required information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **By its byte size**

 
 
• Byte size refers to the **amount of data** that can be stored in a memory cell (typically 8 bits).
 
• While byte size is **important for data representation**, it does not help in distinguishing between individual memory cells.
 
 
 
• **By its capacity**
 
 
• Capacity refers to the total amount of** data that can be stored** in memory (e.g., 4GB, 8GB).
 
• Capacity is a broader measure and does not specify individual memory locations.
 
 
 
• **By its data item**
 
 
• Data items refer to the** type of data stored **(e.g., integer, character).
 
• Different memory cells can store various data items, but this does not provide a unique identifier for each cell.

questions.question: In PPT What method can be used to move among slides if your hands are already on the keyboard?

options.text: Pressing the Esc key to exit the presentation
Clicking on the slide thumbnail in the Slides tab

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Using the keyboard directional keys.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** keyboard directional keys (left and right arrows)** allow you to **move between slides** quickly without taking your hands off the keyboard.
 
• This method is convenient for presenters who want to maintain focus on their presentation **without needing to use a mouse or touchpad.**
 
• You can use the up and down arrow keys** to navigate through the slides** in a more controlled manner, allowing for smooth transitions.
 
• This method works in various presentation software, including **Microsoft PowerPoint**, making it a universally applicable technique.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pressing the Esc key to exit the presentation**

 
 
• The Esc key is used to **exit the presentation mode** rather than navigate between slides.
 
• This action interrupts the flow of the presentation, making it unsuitable for moving among slides.
 
 
 
• **Scrolling with the mouse wheel**
 
 
• While you can **scroll through slides in editing mode**, this method is not effective during an actual presentation.
 
• Presenters typically do not use the mouse wheel for navigation in slideshow mode.
 
 
 
• **Clicking on the slide thumbnail in the Slides tab**
 
 
• This method requires you to use the mouse, which goes against the premise of keeping your hands on the keyboard.
 
• It is more appropriate for **editing or organizing slides **rather than during a live presentation

questions.question: The cell wall of bacteria is made up of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **peptidoglycan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Peptidoglycan is a **polymer that provides structural support** to the bacterial cell wall, helping maintain its shape and integrity.
 
• It is **composed of sugars and amino acids,** forming a mesh-like structure that is unique to bacteria.
 
• The amount and structure of peptidoglycan in the cell wall determine whether bacteria are classified as** Gram-positive or Gram-negative**, affecting their response to antibiotics.
 
• The cell wall protects bacteria from **osmotic pressure and environmental stresses**, making it crucial for their survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glycogen**

 
 
• Glycogen is a storage** form of glucose in animals and fungi,** not found in bacterial cell walls.
 
• It is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units, primarily used for energy storage.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose**
 
 
• Cellulose is a major **component of plant cell walls**, providing structural support.
 
• It is not a structural component of bacterial cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Peptone**
 
 
• Peptone is a **protein digest used in culture media for growing bacteria**, but it is not a component of the bacterial cell wall.
 
• It is made from the digestion of proteins and provides nutrients for bacteria in laboratory settings.

questions.question: Intervention by the monetary authority of a country in the money market to keep money supply stable against exogenous or sometimes external shocks is called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sterilisation**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Intervention by the monetary authority of a country in the money market to keep money supply stable against exogenous or sometimes external shocks is referred to as **sterilisation**.
 
• The primary goal of sterilisation is to neutralize the effects of capital flows on the domestic money supply.
 
• This is achieved by offsetting foreign exchange interventions with domestic monetary operations.
 
• For instance, when a central bank buys foreign currency to prevent the appreciation of the local currency, it can sell government bonds to absorb the resulting increase in the money supply.
 
• Without sterilisation, such interventions could lead to inflation or other economic imbalances.
 
• Therefore, sterilisation helps in maintaining monetary stability and controlling inflation.

questions.question: In a test match, the captain of the fielding side may demand a new ball after _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**80 overs**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to the rules of cricket, specifically in Test matches, the fielding captain can request a new ball after 80 overs have been bowled.
 
• The batting team has the option to decline the new ball if they choose to, but this is rare as most teams prefer to take advantage of the fresh ball.
 
• The new ball can be beneficial as it offers bowlers a chance to generate more swing and bounce, making it easier to dismiss batsmen.
 
• However, the team must still have bowled 80 overs to be eligible for the new ball.
 
• Fast bowlers often prefer the new ball as it can bounce more and may swing in the air, leading to more opportunities for dismissals.
 
• Spinners, however, may prefer the old ball, which is softer and easier to grip, allowing for more turn

questions.question: The Big Dipper is an asterism formed by the seven brightest stars in the constellation:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ursa Major**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Big Dipper is an asterism made up of the seven brightest stars** in the constellation Ursa Major: 
 
• **The Big Dipper is a well-known pattern of stars that's part of the Ursa Major constellation.**
 
• It's always visible because it's circumpolar, meaning it's in the same direction as the North Star.
 
• The Big Dipper is a useful navigational tool because it points to the North Star, which is a celestial pivot point.
 
• To find the North Star, you can extend an imaginary line through the front two stars of the Big Dipper, Merak and Dubhe. 
 
• The Big Dipper is also known by other names, including:
 
 
• The Plough, Charles's Wain, Septentriones, and The Wagon. 
 
 
 
• The Big Dipper is a prominent asterism in the Ursa Major constellation, which is significant in many cultures.
 
• In Native American traditions, the stars of Ursa Major are thought to mark the changing seasons and guide spirits

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Leo Major
 
 
• Likely refers to Leo, a constellation in the night sky, sometimes called "Leo the Lion."
 
• Leo Major may be an informal way of distinguishing Leo from the smaller constellation Leo Minor.
 
• Leo is one of the 12 zodiac constellations and is visible primarily during the spring in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
 
 
• Cassiopeia
 
 
• Cassiopeia is a prominent constellation in the northern sky, named after the mythical queen of Ethiopia in Greek mythology.
 
• It is easily recognizable by its distinctive W or M shape, formed by five bright stars.
 
• Cassiopeia is visible year-round in the Northern Hemisphere and is often used to locate other celestial objects.
 
 
 
• Orion
 
 
• Orion, also known as "The Hunter," is one of the most recognizable and famous constellations.
 
• It features prominent stars like Betelgeuse and Rigel, as well as the Orion Belt, formed by three aligned stars (Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka).
 
• Orion is best visible during winter in the Northern Hemisphere and has deep mythological and cultural significance.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Akbar__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahabharata was translated into Persian at Akbar’s orders, by Faizi and `Abd al-Qadir Bada’uni__ (c. 1540 – 1615) and named Razmnameh.
 
• Akbar
 __
 
• Akbar was the third Mughal emperor, who reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• Akbar succeeded his father, Humayun.
 
• Jahangir was his son.
 
• His abolition of Jajiya, his new religion Din-i-Ilahi, his land revenue policy, administrative policy etc. were such that his half century rule proved to be one of the brightest chapters in Indian History
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jahangir

 
 
• Jahangir was a great patron of art and literature he spent lavishly in building splendid buildings and gardens and mausoleums.
 
• He was easily impressed by poets and writers especially those who wrote verses in his praise.
 
• Under his rule, he got constructed the Akbar's tomb, Idmaat ud Daulas tomb, and the famous Jahangir Fort.
 
 
 
• Aurangzeb
 
 
• Aurangzeb was the last important Mughal ruler and after him, the Mughal empire rapidly decayed and was finally put to an end by the British.
 
• This King reigned for half a century and died in 1707 leaving behind a war of succession.
 
 
 
• Humayun
 
 
• Humayun was the second emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled over territory in what is now Afghanistan, Pakistan, Northern India, and Bangladesh from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NRLM aims to reduce poverty by promoting **self-employment **and organization of rural poor into self-help groups (SHGs).
 
• The mission focuses on marginalized and disadvantaged groups, including** Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), **and** women**, to enhance their livelihood opportunities.
 
• NRLM emphasizes skill development and capacity building, facilitating training programs to enhance employability and entrepreneurial skills among rural youth.
 
• The mission promotes sustainable livelihoods through various sectors, including **agriculture, animal husbandry, **and** rural crafts**, to improve income levels and enhance quality of life in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana (AGEY)**

 
 
• **AGEY **aims to provide rural livelihood opportunities by facilitating the operation of village-level transport services to improve connectivity and access to markets.
 
• The initiative encourages **self-employment** by supporting individuals or groups to operate transport vehicles, promoting local entrepreneurship in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Aajeevika Skills**
 
 
• Aajeevika Skills focuses on providing skill training to **rural youth** through the establishment of **skill development** centers to enhance their employability in various sectors.
 
• The program collaborates with various industries to ensure that the training aligns with market needs, enabling better job placements for trainees.
 
 
 
• **Self-Employment through Aajeevika**
 
 
• This initiative encourages the formation of micro-enterprises by providing **financial assistance**, mentorship, and capacity-building support to rural entrepreneurs.
 
• It helps connect self-employed individuals with markets by facilitating access to technology, market information, and business development services.
 
 
 
• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM)**
 
 
• DAY-NRLM focuses on promoting sustainable livelihoods by organizing rural poor into** self-help groups** (SHGs) and facilitating access to credit and financial services.
 
• The scheme provides skill development and training programs to enhance the employability of **rural youth** and empower them to start their own businesses.

questions.question: Shattantri Veena, meaning a Veena with hundred strings, is the ancient Sanskrit name of which instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Santoor is a hammered dulcimer from the family of **string instruments**.
 
• The Santoor is primarily associated with **Indian classical music**, especially in the Hindustani tradition.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma** has received the Padma Vibhushan and Padma Shri for their contributions to music.
 
• Santoor has gained popularity in contemporary and **fusion music** genres, showcasing its versatility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarod**

 
 
• A **fretless** string instrument with a deep, rich sound, typically made of wood and played with a plectrum.
 
• Renowned players include **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan** and **Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, **who have popularized the Sarod in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• A **bowed** string instrument known for its emotional expressiveness, often used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Traditionally associated with vocal music accompaniment; famous players include **Ustad Sultan Khan** and **Pandit Ram Narayan**.
 
 
 
• **Tambura/Tanpura**
 
 
• A **long-necked** string instrument used primarily as a drone in Indian classical music, providing a harmonic foundation.
 
• Renowned musicians like **Ustad Vilayat Khan** and **Pandit Ravi Shankar** have included the Tanpura in their performances.

questions.question: What kind of a satellite is CMS-01,that was launched by ISRO in December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Communication.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CMS-01** is a communication satellite designed to provide various communication services across India, particularly in the areas of telecommunication, broadcasting, and broadband.
 
• The satellite is intended to serve the Indian subcontinent, enhancing connectivity and communication infrastructure in remote and rural areas.
 
• CMS-01 was launched on **December 17, 2020**, aboard the PSLV-C49 rocket from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota**.
 
• It operates in the **Geostationary Orbit** and is equipped with **12 Ku-band transponders**, enabling high-quality communication services and data transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **INSAT Series**

 
 
• It was designed for telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and search and rescue operations.
 
• The series includes **multiple satellites** that provide critical data for weather forecasting and disaster management.
 
 
 
• **IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) Satellites**
 
 
• It was primarily for **earth observation** and resource management, including agriculture, forestry, and land-use mapping.
 
• Usage: Data from IRS satellites supports planning and monitoring of natural resources and environmental management.
 
 
 
• **NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation)**
 
 
• A regional navigation satellite system providing accurate positioning services to users in India and surrounding regions.
 
• It enhances navigation capabilities and is an alternative to** GPS** for users in India.
 
 
 
• **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)**
 
 
• India's first** interplanetary mission**, designed to explore Mars and gather data on its surface and atmosphere.
 
• It made India the first Asian nation to reach Martian orbit and the fourth space agency globally to do so.
 
 
 
• **GSAT Series**
 
 
• Geostationary satellites designed for providing various communication services including TV broadcasting and internet services.
 
• It enhances** telecommunication infrastructure** and digital connectivity across the country.
 
 
 
• **Astrosat**
 
 
• India’s first dedicated **multi-wavelength space observatory** for astronomical observations.
 
• It enables detailed study of celestial sources across different wavelengths, contributing to advancements in astrophysics.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Warren Hastings became the Governor-General of Bengal from Governor of Bengal after the passing of which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act, of 1773.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It established the office of the **Governor-General of Bengal**, with **Warren Hastings** as the first holder.
 
• It created the **Supreme Court **of Judicature at Calcutta, introducing a formal judicial system.
 
• It increased government oversight of the **British East India Company**'s activities in India.
 
• It formed a Council of** four** members to assist the Governor-General, ensuring checks and balances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt’s India Act, 1784**

 
 
• It established a **dual system of governance**, separating the political and commercial functions of the East India Company.
 
• It created a **Board of Control** to oversee the Company's administration and ensure accountability to the British government.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act, 1813**
 
 
• It renewed the **East India Company's charter** for another 20 years, allowing it to continue its trade.
 
• It ended the Company's monopoly on trade with India, permitting British subjects to trade freely.
 
• It provided for the **promotion of education** and spread of knowledge in India, including the use of English.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council Act of 1861:**
 
 
• The Act recognized the **portfolio system**, which allowed members of the Viceroy's council to oversee specific government departments, marking a shift toward a more organized executive structure.
 
• It restored legislative powers to the** Bombay **and **Madras Presidencies**, reversing centralization that began with the **Regulating Act of 1773**, thus enabling more localized governance.
 
• The Act empowered the** Viceroy** to issue ordinances without legislative council approval during emergencies, allowing for swift governance in urgent situations

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __12-35__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Rights protect individual freedoms and ensure** equality**, **liberty**, and **justice** as enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
 
• They include six main categories, such as the** Right to Equality,** **Right to Freedom**, and **Right against Exploitation**.
 
• Fundamental Rights are** justiciable**, allowing citizens to seek legal recourse for violations through the courts.
 
• These rights are not absolute and can be restricted in the interest of public order, morality, and **national security**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSPs aim to promote social and economic justice by reducing inequalities in income, status, and opportunities. This principle supports the idea of a welfare state.
 
• They direct the State to provide free and compulsory education for children until the age of 14, ensuring that education is accessible to all citizens.
 
• **Right to Work:** The DPSPs include provisions for securing a living wage and decent working conditions for workers, aiming to ensure that everyone has the right to work and earn a livelihood.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties (FD)**
 
 
• **Article 51A **lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens, including the duty to** abide by the Constitution** and **respect** its ideals and institutions, which fosters a sense of responsibility.
 
• **Environmental Protection:** One of the duties includes the responsibility to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, emphasizing the importance of environmental conservation.
 
• **Promotion of Harmony:** The Fundamental Duties encourage citizens to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all people, transcending religious, linguistic, or regional diversities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 12:** Definition of the "**State**".
 
• **Article 13:** It declares that any law or ordinance that is** inconsistent** with the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Constitution shall be deemed **void**.
 
• **Articles 14-18:** Right to equality and prohibition of discrimination.
 
• **Articles 19-22:** Right to freedom, protection against arbitrary arrest, etc.
 
• **Articles 23-24:** Prohibition of trafficking and child labor.
 
• **Articles 25-32:** Freedom of religion and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• **Article 32:** Right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, India’s population accounts _________ of the world’s population.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17.5%.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Census of India conducted in 2011 reported a population of over **1.2 billion**, which contributed to India's significant share of the global population.
 
• The Census reported a gender ratio of** 940** females for every 1,000 males.
 
• According to the 2011 Census,** 31.16% **of India's population lived in urban areas, a significant increase from **27.81%** in **2001**.
 
• The overall literacy rate in India was recorded at **74.04%**, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at **65.46%**.
 
• The first complete census of India was conducted in **1881**, and it was the first synchronous census to be conducted across the entire Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The population of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in India accounted for **16.6%** and **8.6%**, respectively.
 
• The Census revealed that children aged 0-6 years constituted about **13.1%** of the total population.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** emerged as the most populous state, with a population exceeding 199 million.
 
• **Sikkim** was recorded as the least populous state, with a population of just over 610,000.
 
• The Census identified** 122** major languages and **1,599 **other languages spoken across the country.
 
• The urban sex ratio was recorded at **929** females for every 1,000 males, slightly lower than the overall ratio.
 
• The 2011 Census was conducted in two phases: the house listing phase** (April to July 2010)** and the population enumeration phase **(February 9 to 28, 2011).**

questions.question: Fundamental duties were introduced in Part IVA of the Constitution by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Forty-second Amendment Act, 1976.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Forty-second Amendment Act, enacted in 1976 during the **Emergency period**, introduced Fundamental Duties in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 51A** outlines **Eleven** Fundamental Duties that citizens are expected to perform.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was influenced by the provisions in the **Soviet Constitution.**
 
• Fundamental Duties in India are** not enforceable** by the courts, meaning citizens cannot be legally punished for not following them; they are moral responsibilities rather than legal obligations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Year
 Key Features
 
 
 
 

 **1951**
 **First Amendment**: Added restrictions on freedom of speech and allowed land reforms.
 
 

 **1976**
 **Forty-second Amendment:** Introduced Fundamental Duties and altered the preamble.
 
 

 **1978**
 **Forty-fourth Amendment: **Restored the balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs; reduced preventive detention powers.
 
 

 **1985**
 **Eighty-third Amendment: **Provided for the reservation of seats for SC and ST in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
 
 

 **1992**
 **Seventy-third Amendment: **Strengthened Panchayati Raj institutions for local self-government in rural areas.
 
 

 **2002**
 **Eighty-sixth Amendment:** Made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
 

 **2019**
 **One Hundred and First Amendment:** Enhanced reservation for the economically weaker sections among the general category.

questions.question: The Union Cabinet, in Aug 2022, approved the enhancement in the limit of Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) by ________ , with the additional amount being earmarked exclusively for enterprises in hospitality and related sectors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__50,000 crore.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) a part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package in 2020
 
• Its objective is to help businesses including MSMEs to meet their operational liabilities and resume businesses the hit caused by the COVID-19 crisis.
 
• It provides Member Lending Institutions (MLIs), 100 percent guarantee against any losses suffered by them due to non-repayment of the ECLGS funding by borrowers.
 
• The overall ceiling initially was Rs 3 lakh crore which was increased to Rs 4.5 lakh crore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ECLGS is under Department of Financial Services (DFS) in the Ministry of Finance.
 
• The R.O.I. is 9.25 percent for Banks and Financial Institutions and 14 percent for Non-Banking Financial Institutions.
 
• Loans under the ECLGS are collateral-free, backed by a government guarantee.
 
• The scheme is implemented through various scheduled commercial banks, financial institutions, and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
